en: Wuwen traveled south to enter Zhejiang. I first established a friendship with Zhongchuan; later, upon entering the gates of various elder masters, my perception was as swift as a flash of lightning and as fierce as a clap of thunder, such that I saw no Buddhas or patriarchs before my eyes.
Twenty years passed since we parted, and he died before me. I have now read through the records of his three assemblies.

The clouds of Mount Lu soar aloft; the waters of East Lake overflow. Although the tongue that knows no words still remains, there is therein a single phrase that does not reside upon the tip of the tongue.
I pray you, fix a single eye upon this record. Written with hands joined in reverence by Ying during the middle month of autumn in the Guiyou year.
The Way is fundamentally wordless, yet it is through words that the Way is revealed.

Master Wumen did not open his mouth nor move his tongue, yet he turned the Wheel of Dharma three times, and his words filled the world. His successor, Master Kang, did not conceal anything from his father but exposed it all.
Now that this story has circulated, he has requested me to compose a commentary. I said: "If one says that Wumen had words, that is to slander Wumen. If..."

This means that there are no written characters or spoken words of oral karma actually present here. If the reader fixes their eyes upon this, then this entire record will be nothing but superfluous words.
Colophon by Lingyin’s Xuzhou Pudu, winter of the ninth year of the Xiachun era.
Preface to the Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Wumen Heshang:
Recorded Sayings from his Initial Residence at Jianfu Chan Temple in Raozhou.
Record of Sayings from Kai-xian Huazang Chan Monastery on Mount Lu in Nan-kang Prefecture;
Record of Sayings from his Second Residence at Jianfu Monastery in Raozhou;
Minor Ritual Services and Eulogies.
Verse Epilogue (Appendix):
The Discourse Record of Master Wumen.
The Discourse Record of Master Wumen during his initial tenure at Jianfu Chan Temple in Ruzhou.
Compiled by the junior monk Weikang.
In the sixth month of the second year of the Baoyu era, the Master accepted the invitation.
Pointing toward the main gate, he said: "Red lotuses stand before the entrance; green willows wind along the path. The eight characters of 'New Jianfu' have been flung wide open."
One may enter here. Wandering freely throughout the world, I occupy this chamber.
Today, I, this mountain monk, shall open the gates of hell and invite all people of the great earth to create the karma of hell.
To realize the fruit of hell. If there were even one person who attained Buddhahood and became a Patriarch, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment myself.

The *Jianghu Shu* (Rivers and Lakes Commentary) says: "They are maliciously acquainted with each other; they cast evil spells and curses, their entire bodies being nothing but mouths, such that they cannot be reconciled.
The *Dushu* (Commentary on the Separation) says: "The Head Seat merely covers it up."
Ascending the seat, he held up the incense and said:
"This one offering of incense is respectfully offered to extend the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years."
Next, he holds up the incense and says: "This incense cannot be looked upon; it cannot be smelled; it cannot be grasped; it cannot be discarded.
To look at it with a cold eye is truly laughable—a laugh that must last for thirty years.
I burn this in the burner, respectfully offered to the late Great Abbot Xiao’ung, who formerly resided at Guangli Chan Temple on Mount Ayuwang in Qingyuan Prefecture."

To repay the grace of the Dharma-milk, [the Master] took his seat (the questions and answers are not recorded). He then said: "Heaven is high and earth is deep; the sun reaches its zenith and the moon declines.
To 'fully raise' or 'partially raise' [the teaching] is worlds apart. Upāli, you have spent your life only knowing how to put on clothes and eat food.
When you heard others speak of the two words 'Buddha-dharma,' it was like the wind passing over the treetops, or water poured upon a stubborn rock. Today, I shall shatter [your ignorance]."
This fellow with the face-skin is called an "Elder.

He wished to engage in some discussion with you all, but for no reason he has endured the great heat of the fifth and sixth months and traveled two thousand li on a long journey, only to have it all lost at once.
Nevertheless, there is fortunately this staff here. (He picks up the staff and says: "Staff, try and say something! (He strikes once. A world of pure peace.
Be careful not to misquote the words. Again, he cited the three sages: Daowu said, "Whenever I meet a person, I come forth; when I have come forth, I do not act for the sake of others.

Xinghua said, "Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forth; when I have come forth, I immediately act for the sake of others. The Master composed a verse: "Brothers, the capital was not much to quarrel over;
Together they boarded the official boat, each rowing for himself. Rowing on and rowing back, they looked behind them; As before,"
Not departing from the marshy isles of *liao* flowers.
That evening, there was a small *can* (where the questions and answers are not recorded). Raising the oars and hoisting the sails, he steered his bottomless boat across the sea.

With a god-like head and a ghostly face, he employed the Unwritten Seal to examine and verify those from all quarters. Having come from as far as two thousand *li* to dwell upon this mountain, he remains single-mindedly.
He takes up this matter. Holding up his whisk, he says: "Look! Look! The seal-pattern has already been revealed. He makes a single stroke: "The seams of the brocade have already opened.
Whether Buddha, Patriarch, sage, or ordinary person, all are sealed here by this one seal.
It reaches such a point that the entire universe and the great earth are filled with a whistling wind. Suddenly, from among the assembly, someone steps forward and says: "Long..."
"Old man, do not be so alarmed. If I had already realized this samādhi during the era of Vipaśyin Buddha, what then?
With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Yunmen bestowed three blows of the staff upon Dongshan; Huangbo struck Linji with three blows of the staff.
To reduce the hearth while adding more soldiers is to waste salt and vinegar. One does not suffice alone; two do not suffice as a pair.
How many stalks of reeds face the red smartweed! People these days look only at the fishing line."
Ascending the hall for the dedication ceremony: "In daily life there is nothing different; who can discern it when the opportunity arises?

This old house with its collapsing walls and broken eaves, these bricks and rubble scattered here and there—how far removed such a way of appearing in the world for the sake of others is from the truth!
Truly, they are worlds apart. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Dharma-gates of the Buddhas and the essential subtleties of the Patriarchs—last night, the rain falling from the four eaves explained them so thoroughly that not a drop could leak out.
If you all can take responsibility for this here and maintain it here," he shook his hand and said:
"Guess, guess! [The Master] ascends the hall.
A monk asks an ancient worthy, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Worthy replies, 'Has the wheat ripened before the mountain yet?
The Master offers this verse: Since childhood I left my home to dwell by the sun; From leaving home, I have traveled three thousand li on the road. From... [the text continues].
When someone asks for the path by which one has come, turning one’s head reveals it is originally right before one’s eyes.
Opening the furnace to thank the elders, he steps onto the field and ascends the hall. Regarding Vzhou’s “no guest or host” dialogue:
those whose ground is stable and secure speak the moment they open their mouths and step with confidence. But as for those who cannot distinguish east from west or north from south—
It cannot be helped that people will inevitably encroach upon his borders and overstep his boundaries. Under the gate of Jianfu, all are people whose fields and lands are secure and well-guarded.
When they lift the incense ladle and set down the fire tongs, everything is perfectly authentic. Why is this so? Because the official seal of verification is clear and distinct.

The Buddha ascended the hall for his final teaching before entering *nirvāṇa*: "All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; they are of the nature of arising and ceasing. When arising and ceasing have ceased, extinction is bliss.
Old Śākyamuni died right here more than two thousand years ago, and to this day, no one has been able to bring him back to life.
Although Jianfu’s arms may be long and his sleeves short, I shall attempt to bring him back to life for you all. Joining his palms, he said: "His countenance—"
How truly marvelous! Its radiance illuminates the ten directions. Ascending the hall:
"This very mind is Buddha"—the mountains have no layers. "Neither mind nor Buddha"—the waters have no layers.
"Not mind, not Buddha"—the white clouds likewise have no layers. Jianfu announces it thus: upon the bridge at Baling...
Facing Xichuan, he ascended the hall and said:
"One cold, one heat; the common era is right here and now. There is no third or second kind.
Holding up his staff, he said: 'This staff sees that you all are unable to preserve yourselves in accordance with the times.'"
With a thunderous crash, a clap of lightning scatters a gust of wind and rain; thus, the realm of cool clarity is realized.
If, at this point, your spirit is pure and your breath is refreshed such that both cold and heat are forgotten, even this staff will break before I let you go.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Dajue had one ladleful; Moshan had half a ladleful. The jade is naturally flawless, yet it is needlessly carved and polished.
Having many years but no virtue—Old Muzhou. For no reason at all, he forced Yunmen’s leg to break."

Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Venerable Zhaozhou once remarked, 'For this old monk, the morning and evening meals are the only miscellaneous uses for body and mind. The Master composed a verse on this:
Having passed through the Jade Gate, he has long since retired from the army, yet he still beats the drums before others.
He speaks only of horses trampling through fields of wild grass, unaware that his own person is already trapped within a heavy siege."
Ascending the hall: Amidst the clamor and bustle, there is quietude and stillness; not a single thread is stirred.
It is like facing ten thousand enemies—alert, truly alert; lucid, truly lucid. Dharma brothers, whether seizing an elephant or seizing a rabbit, one must exert their full strength in both.
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Early summer grows warm; midsummer is intensely hot. From the beginning of heaven and earth until the present day, there has not been the slightest difference.

If there were a monk with spiritual bone, as soon as he emerged from his mother’s womb, he would have known the seasons and recognized the times—following the fragrant grasses when departing and chasing the falling flowers when returning, fully endowed with seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. He would receive...
By means of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, there is no birth to be guarded against and no restraint to be bound. Nevertheless, it is easy to realize that early summer’s gradual heat is easy;
it is difficult to realize that midsummer’s extreme heat is difficult. It is easy to realize that midsummer’s extreme heat is easy;

it is difficult to realize that early summer’s gradual heat is difficult. Difficult, indeed difficult! Watch for yourself during these ninety days. Again, he raised the instance of the Fifth Patriarch’s commencement of the summer retreat.

The Hall Master said: "Since we have entered the summer retreat, there has been nothing with which to make offerings to the great assembly. I shall therefore prepare a fine banquet to attend to you all.
He then raised his hand and said: "Luo-luo, summon; luo-luo, wave; luo-luo, dismiss. Do not resent my lack of abundance. I humbly pray that you will take care of yourselves. The Master commented:
"Old Dongshan’s dragon-essence and phoenix-marrow were complete with a hundred flavors. Yet, alas, even exquisite food cannot satisfy one who is already full."

People eat it. Ascending the hall, he said: "No talismans are written; no herbs are gathered. To raise the dead and ward off misfortune. He took up his staff and struck once, saying: "Fortunately, this is still here.
Throughout the entire monastery, the summer breeze blows and the days are long. People dwell in a world fragrant with lotus blossoms."
Ascending the hall: The autumn night is deep and long; the dew is cold and the moon is bright. The bell sounds short when it should be short and long when it should be long;
the insects chirp loud when they should be loud and soft when they should be soft. Hearing this, I, the mountain monk, toss and turn, unable to sleep until dawn. Why is this?
A single piece of the Patriarch’s mind—how much of it lies in ruins?
Ascending the hall, a monk asked an ancient worthy, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The worthy replied, “Tear down the eastern fence and patch up the western wall.
The Master commented: “Tear down the eastern fence, patch up the western wall; an eight-cornered caltrops is hurled right before one’s face—the eyes!”
In stillness and movement, one must take up the burden. As before, it is an iron wall, then again an iron wall.

At the Winter Solstice, during the small *sāṃkathya*, he struck once and raised the staff twice, uttering a single phrase. A drop of water gives rise to ice; he cast aside three and let go of two to reveal a single function.
The cliffs collapse and the rocks shatter. Nowhere can it be understood through intellectual comprehension; nowhere can it be grasped through deliberation.
Thus, Jizizi only knew how to step forward and join his palms; Xiangyan only knew how to join his palms and step forward.

If you wish to understand the shifting of the celestial dial and the arrival of the winter solstice, you have not yet grasped it. Holding up his staff, he said: "This staff has always been a dead fox;
tonight, unable to restrain its impatience, it leaps forth with joy, taking the heavens, the earth, and the great world all at once..."
It has been swallowed up. If you can understand it here, then indeed it will ripen upon the head of the shadowless tree.
If this is not yet the case, then beans will burst forth from cold ashes. Again, he raised the case where Master Yuquan addressed the assembly, saying:
"The movement of the sun's shadow shifts; the trousers are bright red. It is not that they are not washed, nor is there a permanent replacement. The Master commented: "Jianfu [should]..."
If you see this at such a time, immediately speak to others and show a little bit of your skill.
On the winter solstice, he ascended the hall; on that day, when the clouds were recorded, he asked, "What color are the clouds? [The answer was: "No sinews in the eyes—blue, yellow, red, and white."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "It has form and substance, yet no beginning or end; it cannot be approached, nor is it easy to avoid.
Great Master Zeng did not see it intimately, and so he mistakenly called it the 'tortoise-nose of the South Mountain.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The superior person, hearing the Way, practices it with diligence. How very urgent they are!

The middling person, hearing the Way, is as if it exists and as if it does not; they still have a slight advantage. The inferior person, hearing the Way, laughs at it—yet this actually possesses the breath of a patch-robed monk.
These three types of people have all been torn apart at once. Now tell me, which of them deserves the offerings of devas and humans?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is nothing difficult about studying the Way; the first requirement is to recognize one's original face.
Nowadays, monks simply spend their winters here and their summers there. When prodded even slightly, most are unable to open their mouths."
Little do you realize that the nostrils, the great head, have always been pointing downward. If you do not believe this, reach out your hand and feel for them yourself.
Entering the hall, he said: "The river moon shines; the pine wind blows. Through the eternal night and clear sky, what is there to do? He looked around at the assembly and said:
If there were such a monk at the Jianfu Gate, I would call him to wash my feet. Why?
Because even for one who is non-active and without affairs, it remains difficult as a golden shackle.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The night is deep as all outflows are exhausted; the wind and dew are profound within the mountain hermitage.

No clouds arise upon the peaks, yet the moon descends into the heart of the waves. Having seen this, the mountain monk truly bites through his teeth and jaw. Why? Because thirty years ago, I too came in just this way."
Ascending the hall: Of the long retreat of one hundred and twenty days, seventy-five have already passed. Regarding past dharmas, each of you has reached their ultimate end;
each has accomplished your task; each has attained purity. As for future dharmas, how should they be treated?
[The Master] sets down his whisk and says: "One should abide in accordance with this."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Shishuang, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shishuang gnashed his teeth to indicate it.
After Shishuang passed away, a monk asked Jiufeng, "What was the intent behind the late master gnashing his teeth?
Jiufeng said, "It would be better to cut out one's tongue than to violate the national taboo. The monk then asked Yungai. Yungai said, "I and the late master have..."
"What a grievous enmity! The Master picked up the case and said: "Do you all wish to know the application of these two elders? 'A son shall conceal for his father;
the rectitude lies right therein.

On ascending the hall to open the furnace, with cold tears dripping from his chin as he sat cross-legged around the brazier, he said: "What need is there to speak of the height of heaven or the vastness of earth?"
The funniest was old Yangqi. He picked up a piece of dead firewood; even before opening his mouth, he had already fallen into a trap.
Entering the hall, he said: "The Way is right before your eyes, with no gaps at all. Whether you go left or right, it hits the mark every time.
Pointing to the banner, he asked: "Is it the wind that moves, or is it the banner?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Linji’s Four Kinds of Discernment and Dongshan’s Four Guest-Host Relationships: 'The sweet melon is sweet all the way to the stem;
the bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. To pour out one's entire heart and entrails to tell them to others is just like rain upon the branches of a plum tree."

On account of the snow, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said that if one were to break into a sweat once for all, one would see jade palaces and crystal halls upon a single blade of grass.
From the past, I have harbored doubts regarding these words; looking at them today, they are indeed true."
Ascending the hall, he ascended Mount Zhi and gazed at the Five Elders. The clouds were still, the sun and moon were upright; his eyes were so lofty that heaven and earth seemed small.
He casually trampled the backbone of Great Master Bodhidharma to pieces and saw the heart, liver, and five viscera of Old Śākyamuni all at once.
Thereupon, reflecting upon this tumultuous world of dust and this vast, boundless universe, he held up a night-bright talisman and asked: "How many know Heaven?"

Dawn. On the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Last night, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara, within the Hall of Good Dharma, together with the Wind Lord and Rain Master, turned the Wheel of Dharma three times and expounded the Buddha-activity of the Lamp-Bright One.
Śākyamuni the Elder, without rising from his seat, realized non-arising."

The Dharma-patience. He personally conferred the prediction of enlightenment upon them. As for all those people on their long rows of beds, with eyes closed and brows shut, when have they ever dreamed of this?
*Recorded Sayings of Master Wumen, Chan Master of Huazang Chan Temple at Kaixian on Mount Lu, Nanjiang Circuit.*
The junior master Weikang compiled the *Index to the Three Gates*.
"Having no place of entry" drives people to exhaustion; "having a place of entry" obstructs people to death.
[The Master] snaps his fingers once and says: "The heavy barrier has been shattered! From where does the single character 'entry' (入) come?"
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: The great ocean of the Flower Treasury is vast and boundless. Rivers, streams, brooks, and rivulets flow into it, all losing their original names.
Fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs swim within it, all losing their original natures. Within this, the Buddhas of the three periods of time realize equal and perfect enlightenment;
within this, all sentient beings drift through the cycle of birth and death. To the assembly gathered here before me:
Within this, one achieves effortless cultivation (*anābhoga-śikṣā*). [The Master] picks up his staff, strikes once, and says:
"Kaixian’s staff has sucked it all dry in a single gulp. Where, ultimately, do the Buddhas of the three periods, all sentient beings, and the great assembly before us tread?
After a long silence, he says: "The waves at Caoxi are just like this; countless ordinary people have been drowned."
"Sinking while on land. He then cited Xiangyan: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is the first true poverty.
Last year’s poverty still left enough space to stick a锥 (chui—a small awl); this year’s poverty leaves no room even for the awl itself. The Master commented: "Do you understand?
You have precisely grasped the place where Kaixian itches."
Ascending the hall: Pre-levying fees and incessant urging; before one’s eyes, every matter requires arrangement.

As for the matters of the supreme vehicle of the lineage, how could there be leisure to speak of them? Suddenly, if someone were to say, "The 'Wordless' discourse has fallen," [the assembly would be struck].
[The Master] covered his mouth with his hand and said, "A transgression!

A transgression! He then ascended the hall and said: "Nanquan, at eighteen, already knew how to manage his livelihood; Zhaozhou, at eighteen, already knew how to break up the family and scatter the household.
If I had seen them back then, I would have struck thirty blows to the heels of each of them. Why? Because—"
His family line is naturally of golden bone; there is no need for sandalwood to enter into fine carving.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Zhaozhou visiting the two hermitage masters. The Master offered this verse: The southern branch faces the warmth, the northern branch suffers the cold;
Though the spring breeze is one, it manifests in two ways. Relying on the high tower, do not blow the flute; Let everyone keep their leaning place.
[The Master] looked over the railing.

He ascended the hall and said: "Since entering the summer retreat at Kaixian, I have been unable to engage in idle chatter with you all. Reciting scriptures and entering the room for private instruction have been set aside;
sitting meditation and the end-of-session bell have both been cast away at once. To attain such freedom—to attain such [liberation]..."
Free and untrammeled. If the Buddha-dharma were not manifest before me, this mountain monk would enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
Ascending the hall: Five days of wind, ten days of rain; the river surface is undisturbed, and the border watchtowers raise no alarms.
Before our eyes, peace gradually dawns; by our ears, we hear much pleasant speech. The mountain man simply gazes at the green mountains; having a mouth, there is no need to swallow it whole.
Buddhas and Patriarchs.

While looking at the *Qingmiao Jing* (Sutra of the Green Sprouts) and expressing thanks for the day’s presiding seat, he ascended the hall and said: "The essential teachings spoken by all Buddhas are like rice, hemp, grain, and millet.
If you can chew through every single word and phrase, you will find an end to hunger and emptiness, and your enjoyment of them will never be exhausted. Such is it.
[The Master] spoke. Since Kaixian had encountered those of the highest caliber, he too brought this forth. Spreading his two hands, he said: "Today is precisely the first day of the sixth month;
it is the end of the summer retreat. He cited an old master who, for an entire summer, did not speak a word to the monks. The Master offered a verse, saying: "Once a word has been uttered..."
Four horses cannot overtake it; once the Way is realized, how can one regret it? Coldly exposed by others, the jaw is clenched fast and the mouth is too weary to open.
Entering the hall: "I meet you at the head of Wushan Ridge; I meet you at the triple gate; I meet you before the Sangha Hall."
To meet you face-to-face—this old man Xuefeng has already wasted salt and sauce.
Nowadays, when monks enter the gate, ascend the hall, and meet their host, they stubbornly clasp their hands at their chests and further demand instruction on a point of entry.
To chew bitter yellow gallus with its very root is not yet the ultimate suffering.
Winter Solstice Small Sermon: When water droplets form ice, one must not yet cease; when cliffs crumble and rocks split, it is precisely the time to advance.
Even if you understand that "one line grows," you have not yet understood that "one line grows";
even if you understand that "one line grows," you have not yet understood that "one line is long. Therefore, while the local dialects may be similar, the prefectures and counties differ. Kaixian—
It is not so. In a state of constant bustle and haste, from the morning cock to the evening bell, one calls winter summer and summer winter.
Who can manage the lengthening or shortening of that single thread? Where the snow and frost have ended, there is the spring breeze. Again, it is cited:

A monk asked an ancient worthy, "After the winter solstice, by how much does the day grow longer? The ancient worthy said, "By a single thread. Another monk then asked a different ancient worthy about the growth of the day.

"About how much? An ancient worthy said, "A single thread of length. The Master took up the point and said: "Traveling the same path beneath the mountain together, each person sees a different landscape before their eyes."
Ascending the hall due to the snow: When you gaze until empty space shatters to pieces, the flowers of emptiness may fly before your eyes at will.
If you still seek elsewhere for a method to settle the mind, the traveler’s road is so vast and long—where will you return?
The Buddha ascended the hall for his final sermon on Nirvana: "Today there is; tomorrow there will be no more. How high is heaven? How deep is earth?
To say that I have entered extinction, or to say that I have not entered extinction—this is but a single corpse, left in such great disarray.
As I observe the assembly of a million followers on Vulture Peak, only Pāpīyān possesses the breath of a true man. Why? Because a flushed face is not as good as the words.
Zhi. Ascending the hall, he said: "Linji’s single shout and Deshan’s single blow are like a thunderclap and a flash of lightning—how could one ever hope to approach them?
Nevertheless, if we speak of the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school, where would they even begin to reach it?"
Master Xun addressed the assembly from the high seat. Master Yu of Taling said: "I have a bright pearl, long confined by the dust of worldly toil;
today the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, piercing through the myriad peaks of mountains and rivers. The Master commented:
"Master Yu has caught a glimpse of something before the donkey and behind the horse, and he immediately exaggerates and flaunts it as his lifelong achievement."
To study the Way. He brandishes his staff, strikes once, and says, "Kaixian has smashed it all to pieces with a single blow. He looks around and asks, "Is there anyone who is not satisfied?
He leans his staff against [the seat] and descends from the platform.
Xie Baoyan ascended the hall and said: "Without stirring a single realm, without revealing a single device—like brocade wrapping a raw stone, or cotton padding a scale-weight.
When Kaixian saw this, he was moved to adorn it with a hundred jewels and wear it upon his head. Why is this? Those who act as ghosts do not recognize it;
those who possess no mind do not yet know it."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "When the sky is clear, cover the roof; when the time comes, reap the grain. Having paid the king’s tax, one beats the belly and sings songs.
The Master added: "Who does not know how to hit a clean ball? Kaixian, however, says otherwise: 'When the sky is clear, cover the roof;
when the time comes, reap the grain. Having paid the king’s tax, the affairs of autumn and winter multiply.'"
Hehe. To call out when one cannot turn back—what can be done?
Entering the hall, he said: "The old man Xuefeng went to Touzi three times and visited Dongshan nine times;
his two feet ran on and on without ceasing. He struck his knee once and said: "If, at that time, this news had been placed in his hands, then [the staff]... (he held up his staff).
One may snap it all at once. Do you all wish to know this? In Jiangnan and the Two Zhe regions, spring is cold and autumn is hot.
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, at the memorial service for the late elders who oversaw the construction, [the Master] ascended the hall and said:

"Rolling once through the field of earth and wood, the eye of one's lifelong practice opens wide and clear. The palaces of the Broad Cold Palace have no locks or keys; smash through the skull and go home."
Ascending the hall to pray for rain: "No rain all winter; no rain all spring; the nine regions of the earth are parched and withered.
The heavens are high, and there is no way to cry out. Holding up his staff, he said: "The staff of Kaixian suddenly transforms into the Sky-Walking Dragon King.
Clouds rise in profusion and a great downpour falls. It reaches the point where the withered flourish, the buds burst open, and the sprouts emerge. He struck the staff.
He struck the staff once and said: "To trigger the mechanism, one must have a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jun weight.
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall, held up his whisk, and said: "Fat, yet no surplus flesh; thin, yet no exposed bone.
It moves the earth and radiates light; its eyes are dark and piercing. Having seen this, even I, this mountain monk, cannot help but join my palms in praise—and say: 'It is not so.'"
The mind is neither Buddha nor a thing.
Recorded sayings of Master Wumen during his second tenure at Jianfu Chan Temple in Raoyou,
compiled by his junior disciple Weikang.

That evening’s informal discourse: "Going, going—yet truly not going; this Dharma abides in its own station. Coming, coming—yet truly not coming; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant.
This mountain monk has counted the years on my fingers and returned once more to Donghu. The lotus leaves are withered, no longer bearing their rain-shielding canopies;
Yet the spring breeze still lingers at the tips of the willow branches. There is not a single hair’s breadth of the phenomenon of coming and going; There is not a single hair’s breadth of the new."

"Old Shangguan: When seen, it is seen by all people together; when heard, it is heard by all people together. Suddenly, there comes forth a man who says, 'Wuwen used the property of the monastery as his own. This is indeed something that has existed [among us]; you are truly, truly too silent! Dahui replies to Elder Zhushan of Dachen:
To consider what one has attained as sufficient and to give rise to mad words and mad actions is indeed a great affliction for those who study the Way.
Even with a spiritual friend such as the former Dahui, and with a practitioner of the Way as diligent as you, Elder Zhushan, one still cannot avoid this fault. Lately...

The Way of the World’s Teacher has not been clarified; the spirit of the scholars has grown increasingly debased. Though they have not yet seen gods or ghosts, they already dance their madness within the forest of the monasteries.
Like those afflicted by wind-disease or who have lost their minds, they are beyond remedy. Those who contemplate this book may perhaps find some measure of healing.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Wumen (End)
